articles.title: Woman killed, 3 injured as Russian attack hits Kyiv residential building, subway station
articles.summary: 'Those who destroyed must pay': Macron's warning to France rioters; 2,400 arrested A Russian air strike killed a woman and injured three others in
articles.body: 'Those who destroyed must pay': Macron's warning to France rioters; 2,400 arrestedA Russian air strike killed a woman and injured three others in Ukraine’s capital, Kyiv, overnight, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Monday. The attack hit a subway station on the city’s left bank and damaged a 25-storey residential building, along with non-residential buildings and a medical facility.Klitschko confirmed the casualties and damage in a statement on Telegram, as Russian attacks continued to threaten civilian infrastructure in the capital, according to Reuters.The strike came amid ongoing efforts to secure a diplomatic settlement to the war, which began with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.Also Read: 'Those who destroyed must pay': Macron's warning to France rioters; 2,400 arrestedUs resumes intelligence sharing with ukraineThe attack comes after the United States resumed sharing critical intelligence with Ukraine following a brief pause, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. The intelligence helps Ukrainian forces detect and prepare for incoming Russian missile strikes, providing vital early warnings against fast-moving threats.Zelenskyy also spoke with US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner after their visit to Kyiv earlier this month.The US administration is seeking to broker an agreement to end the war, which has continued since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.You use AI every day. articles.title: City halls torched, shops looted: France in shock after violent protest - videos
articles.summary: France witnessed widespread destruction, looting and clashes with police as nationwide protests over the rising cost of living and poor conditions in
articles.body: France witnessed widespread destruction, looting and clashes with police as nationwide protests over the rising cost of living and poor conditions in schools escalated into violence, leaving businesses damaged and public buildings in flames. President Emmanuel Macron has vowed legal action against rioters while announcing measures to address public grievances.The scale of the unrest was visible in Paris on Sunday, where shattered shopfronts, broken glass and dislodged cobblestones littered the area around Place de la République. Videos across social media sites also showed damage and looting in other shopping and tourist districts.Authorities estimated that around 5,50,000 people took part in Saturday’s demonstrations, while organisers put the turnout at 8,00,000. The protests were backed by labour unions, student organisations and activists seeking to revive the “yellow vest” movement, which emerged in 2018 over social injustice.Macron vows action as arrests mountIn a televised address, Macron acknowledged the public’s “anger” and “shame” over the unrest, while drawing a distinction between peaceful demonstrators and those involved in violence.“Those who looted will have to pay for the damage, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable,” Macron said.He also condemned what he described as “unrestrained violence” by “insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals.”Social media has been flooded with viral videos of burning buildings, smashed storefronts and clashes, with users declaring “France has fallen” and warning that the country is on the brink.At least 2,400 people were arrested, according news agency AP. Macron said he had instructed prefects to work with mayors to protect public buildings and businesses, including by banning protests where necessary.City halls set ablaze, businesses lootedIn Limoges, flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall on Saturday, causing its roof to collapse and nearly destroying the building. Haute-Vienne prefect Maurice Barate said “radical troublemakers” had broken in while officials, employees, security personnel and members of the public were inside.“They deliberately set the building on fire. It is an extremely serious and unspeakable act,” Barate said.In Marseille, protesters briefly entered the City Hall lobby, while a group damaged a police station. In Lyon, a fire broke out inside a tourist office.Paris mayor Emmanuel Grégoire described the damage as “considerable and unprecedented”, while stressing that the capital must remain a place where people can demonstrate and businesses can operate safely.Political blame and economic concernsThe unrest has also fuelled political tensions ahead of next spring’s presidential election. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen criticised Macron’s government, while left-wing leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon condemned looting and destruction.US president Donald Trump posted “France is burning!” on Truth Social, blaming immigration fro the protets and called on the country to “Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!” French authorities have not linked immigrants to the rioting.The unrest also weighed on the euro in Asian trading on Monday. The currency fell 0.1% to $1.1225, while the dollar index held at 101.83, Reuters reported.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US Immigration authorities return Indian national to Oregon jail over crash that killed newlywed couple
articles.summary: US authorities have transferred 32-year-old Indian national Rajinder Kumar to state custody in Oregon to face prosecution over a November 2025
articles.body: US authorities have transferred 32-year-old Indian national Rajinder Kumar to state custody in Oregon to face prosecution over a November 2025 tractor-trailer crash that killed two newlywed Americans, the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said.Kumar has been indicted in Deschutes County, Oregon, on two counts of first-degree manslaughter and three counts of recklessly endangering another person. The charges remain pending before the state court, and the allegations have not been established at trial.In a post on X on Sunday, October 18, ICE's Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) Seattle office confirmed Kumar's transfer to the Deschutes County Jail, saying the move would allow state criminal proceedings to continue.“Two Americans lost their lives, and their families deserve accountability,” ICE ERO Seattle Acting Field Office Director Julio S Hernandez said, according to the agency's official statement.“ICE worked closely with law-enforcement partners to ensure Kumar is returned to state custody to answer for the serious charges against him,” Hernandez added, according to ANI.He further said, “This coordinated action protects the public, supports the victims’ families, and ensures that an individual accused of these crimes does not evade justice.”“ICE will continue using every lawful tool available to protect the American people from criminal activity committed by illegal aliens,” Hernandez said.According to ICE, the agency had lodged an immigration detainer with the Deschutes County Jail following Kumar's earlier arrest. However, the county released him in April 2026 without honouring the detainer, the agency said.“ICE officers subsequently located and arrested Kumar at large earlier this year,” the agency said in its post, without specifying the date or location of his subsequent arrest.ICE said deportation proceedings would remain on hold until the conclusion of the state criminal case. “Following the conclusion of state criminal proceedings, ICE will pursue Kumar’s immigration case consistent with federal law,” it said.The agency's statement also outlined Kumar's immigration history. According to ICE, US Border Patrol apprehended him near Lukeville, Arizona, on November 28, 2022, after he “illegally entered the United States from Mexico”.He was subsequently placed in removal proceedings. ICE said that “a pending application does not confer legal status in the United States”.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Weather tomorrow: IMD forecasts rain in several states including Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh; 17 Tamil Nadu districts under yellow alert
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast widespread rainfall across several parts of south India on Tuesday, October 20, with
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast widespread rainfall across several parts of south India on Tuesday, October 20, with Kerala, South Interior Karnataka and Tamil Nadu likely to receive showers. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are also expected in parts of the region, while isolated very heavy rainfall is likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal.The IMD has issued a yellow alert for 17 districts of Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Cuddalore and Tiruchi, until October 23. Rainfall activity is expected to continue across several parts of south India over the coming days, with some areas likely to experience heavy showers.Northwest, central, eastern and northeastern India are expected to see no significant weather activity during the week, according to the IMD forecast.IMD weather alert for TuesdayFairly widespread to widespread rainfall is likely over Kerala and Mahe, Lakshadweep, South Interior Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on Tuesday.Coastal Karnataka is also likely to receive rainfall, while North Interior Karnataka, Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam, Rayalaseema and Telangana may see isolated to scattered showers.Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph, are likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal. Similar conditions are expected over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema.Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep and parts of Karnataka may experience gusty winds reaching 30-40 kmph, with gusts up to 50 kmph.Tamil Nadu weather tomorrowTamil Nadu is likely to remain under an active spell of rainfall on Tuesday, with isolated very heavy showers forecast over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal during October 19-21.The IMD has issued a yellow alert for 17 districts of Tamil Nadu until October 23, including Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Cuddalore and Tiruchi.Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph, are likely in parts of the state. Heavy rainfall is also expected at isolated places from October 22 to 24, indicating that wet conditions may persist through the week.Residents in the districts under alert should follow official weather updates and exercise caution during thunderstorms and periods of intense rainfall.Kerala and Lakshadweep weather forecastKerala and Mahe are likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall on Tuesday, with isolated heavy rainfall forecast during October 19-24.Lakshadweep is also likely to experience widespread rainfall during the period, with isolated heavy showers expected from October 21 to 23.Gusty winds reaching 30-40 kmph, with gusts up to 50 kmph, are likely over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep on October 19-20. Isolated thunderstorms and lightning are also possible over these regions on October 21-22.Karnataka weather tomorrowSouth Interior Karnataka is likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall on Tuesday, with isolated heavy rainfall forecast during October 19-24.North Interior Karnataka may see isolated to scattered showers throughout the period. Gusty winds reaching 30-40 kmph, with gusts up to 50 kmph, are likely over both North and South Interior Karnataka on October 19-20.Coastal Karnataka is expected to receive rainfall on October 19-20, with isolated to scattered showers possible on October 21-22. Rainfall activity is forecast to increase again on October 23-24.Andhra Pradesh and Telangana weatherCoastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam, along with Rayalaseema, are likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall on Tuesday. The IMD has forecast isolated heavy rainfall in these regions during October 19-21.Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph, are likely on October 19-20. Gusty winds reaching 30-40 kmph, with gusts up to 50 kmph, may continue on October 21-22.Strong surface winds are also likely over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema during October 19-22.Telangana may receive isolated to scattered showers during October 19-21, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds.Weather forecast for northwest, central, east and northeast IndiaNo significant weather activity is likely over northwest, central, eastern, western and northeastern India during the week, according to the IMD.The forecast indicates that the main rainfall activity will remain concentrated over south peninsular India, particularly Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and parts of Andhra Pradesh.IMD forecast for the next few daysRainfall is likely to continue across several parts of south India through October 24.Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal may experience very heavy rainfall at isolated places until October 21, followed by heavy showers during October 22-24. Kerala and Mahe, as well as South Interior Karnataka, are also likely to receive isolated heavy rainfall through October 24.Lakshadweep may see heavy rainfall during October 21-23, while Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and Rayalaseema are likely to experience isolated heavy showers until October 21.With thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds expected in several areas, residents are advised to monitor IMD updates, particularly in districts covered by weather alerts.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Japan’s MMX moon mission to launch on Oct 20, bring Phobos samples back by 2031
articles.summary: A Japanese space mission is set to lift off on October 20 with an ambitious goal: collect a sample from Phobos, one of Mars’ two moons, and bring it back
articles.body: A Japanese space mission is set to lift off on October 20 with an ambitious goal: collect a sample from Phobos, one of Mars’ two moons, and bring it back to Earth for detailed scientific analysis.If successful, the mission will mark the first time material from Mars or either of its moons has been brought back to Earth.Led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), the Mars Moons Exploration (MMX) mission is expected to reach the Martian neighbourhood in August 2027. Scientists hope the mission will help resolve a long-standing question about the origins of Phobos and Deimos.The MMX spacecraft will study Deimos while travelling through the Martian system before turning its attention to Phobos. The mission will deploy a small rover to survey the moon’s rocky terrain and help identify a suitable landing site for the main spacecraft.“No one has ever landed a rover on such a small moon,” Russell said, explaining that the competing gravitational influences make it difficult to place a rover safely on the surface.After the rover surveys the terrain, the spacecraft will descend onto Phobos and use a robotic arm and two sampling devices to collect material from the surface.The mission aims to gather approximately 10 grams of moon dust. The material will be sealed in a capsule and transported back to Earth, with the return scheduled for 2031. The capsule is expected to land in South Australia’s Woomera region.How did Mars get its moons?One of the mission’s primary objectives is to determine how Phobos and Deimos formed. Scientists are currently considering two leading explanations.According to the first theory, a large object struck Mars billions of years ago, scattering debris into space that eventually formed the two moons. The alternative explanation suggests that Phobos and Deimos were asteroids travelling through the Solar System before Mars captured them through its gravitational pull.Researchers expect the returned material’s chemical and mineral composition to help distinguish between the two possibilities.“When we get the sample back, we'll be able to look in detail at its chemistry and its mineral composition - and the two hypotheses will produce very distinct results,” Russell said.Scientists have long sought to study samples collected directly from Mars and its surroundings, as laboratory analysis can reveal details that spacecraft instruments may not be able to establish conclusively.The MMX spacecraft is scheduled to launch from Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center at 4:41 am local time on October 20.You use AI every day.
